CREATE TABLE SPENDING (
    USER_ID INT,
    SPEND_DATE DATE,
    PLATFORM ENUM('DESKTOP', 'MOBILE'),
    AMOUNT INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (USER_ID, SPEND_DATE, PLATFORM),
    CHECK (AMOUNT > 0),
    CHECK (PLATFORM IN ('DESKTOP', 'MOBILE'))
);
explanation: Both queries aim to produce, per spend date, totals and user counts for three mutually exclusive buckets: Desktop-only, Mobile-only, and Both. Q1 classifies each (date, user) via a nested IF and then counts users per bucket after joining against a generated (date x category) set. However, Q1’s classifier falls back to 'DESKTOP' when both per-user, per-date platform totals are zero (IF(MOBILE_AMOUNT > 0, ..., 'DESKTOP')). Thus, if a (user, date) aggregates to DA = 0 and MA = 0, Q1 will still place that user in 'DESKTOP' and count them. Q2, on the other hand, uses explicit predicates (DA>0 AND MA=0, etc.) and will not count a user whose DA and MA are both zero in any bucket. explanation: Both queries aim to compute day-1 retention by install date (first login date). CREATE TABLE SPENDING (
    USER_ID INT,
    SPEND_DATE DATE,
    PLATFORM ENUM('DESKTOP', 'MOBILE'),
    AMOUNT INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (USER_ID, SPEND_DATE, PLATFORM),
    CHECK (AMOUNT > 0),
    CHECK (PLATFORM IN ('DESKTOP', 'MOBILE'))
);
explanation: Both queries want per-day totals split into three report buckets: DESKTOP-only users, MOBILE-only users, and BOTH (users who used both platforms that day). Q1 correctly derives a per-(date,user) platform bucket, then LEFT JOINs to a scaffold of all (date, platform) report buckets and aggregates, so it always returns 3 rows per date. Q2 tries to do the same via a RIGHT JOIN to the same scaffold, but it has two issues: (1) the inner subquery A selects PLATFORM without grouping by it (MySQL loose-grouping), and (2) the outer GROUP BY uses unqualified column names (GROUP BY SPEND_DATE, PLATFORM) while both sides of the RIGHT JOIN provide those columns. This typically binds GROUP BY to the B-side columns; for scaffold rows with no match on B, those grouping keys are NULL, so all unmatched (date, platform) combinations collapse into a single (NULL, NULL) group. As a result, Q2 returns fewer rows (collapsed zero-match groups), while Q1 returns one row per (date, platform) combination.

With Q1, you still get 3 rows per date (zeros where no users). With Q2, due to RIGHT JOIN and unqualified GROUP BY binding to the left side, all unmatched buckets group as (NULL, NULL) and collapse into one row, making Q2’s result set have fewer rows than Q1’s.
